newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: UN says seven oil contracts approved for Iraq.
newsitem.headline: UN says seven oil contracts approved for Iraq.

text.p: The United Nations has approved seven oil contracts for Iraq since the oil-for-food deal began a week ago, U.N. spokeswoman Sylvana Foa said on Tuesday.
Foa did not give details on the contracts, which were approved by overseers or oil experts hired by the United Nations.

The oil-for-food plan allows Iraq to sell $2 billion worth of oil over six months to buy food and medicine for its people suffering under sanctions imposed when Baghdad's troops invaded Kuwaiti in August 1990.
Contracts approved previously by the United Nations for delivery of Iraqi crude involved the following companies, volumes of oil and duration:

Turkish state oil company TUPRAS received approval for 75,000 barrels per day (bpd) over six months; U.S. Coastal Corp for 60,000 bpd over six months; U.S. Bayoil for 30,000 bpd over six months; France's Elf-Aquitaine for 30,000 bpd over six months; Italy's Oil Energy for 10,000 bpd over three months; and Dutch-company Trafigura for 20,000 bpd over three months.
Details on the contracts were gathered from industry and diplomatic sources.
Iraq's State Oil Marketing Organisation (SOMO) said more contracts have been signed with oil companies, but have yet to go through the approval process at the United Nations.
